reason: Verified in source and at runtime; every load-bearing measurement holds. shell.css:50-61 declares the ladder as size-bound and says in its own comment that it exists to end 'the same 20px string tracked two ways on two surfaces' - and b.css breaks exactly that. Measured computed styles across 11 states x 390/768/1280/1440: Geist 24px renders at both -0.015em (.b-title raised 17->24px by b.css:718 with no re-track) and -0.03em (.b-dayNowTitle, b.css:666); Geist 30px renders at both -0.015em (.b-when raised 20->30px by b.css:707) and -0.03em (.b-endedTitle, b.css:671); Geist Mono 15px renders at both 0.04em (.b-away) and 0em (.b-step, b.css:451-458, mono with no letter-spacing where the ladder assigns --track-data). All eight named 15/17px sans rules carry no letter-spacing at all (.b-gapNote 100, .b-behindNote 286, .b-dayNote 664, .b-bubble 574, .b-undoAct 505, .b-emptyBody 530, .b-endedBody 679, .b-pressBody 549) while every sibling string at the same size carries --track-body. The flagship owner-flight screen at 1440 is the proof: '.b-sub Wedding day at The Orchard' computes 15px/-0.225px and '.b-gapNote Nothing is planned until 1 August.' computes 15px/normal, one column apart on the same screen (the finding says 40px apart; measured tops are 409 and 496 with the today rule between - looser than stated, but the two-letterfits-at-one-size defect is exactly as described). In the min-width:701px block seven rules raise a size (.b-num, .b-when, .b-away, .b-title, .b-emptyTitle, .b-dayNames, .b-pressTitle) and only .b-pressTitle re-tracks (b.css:724); .b-emptyTitle lands at 64px still wearing --track-head and .b-dayNames at 96px still wearing --track-title. This is not something the gates prove: audit.mjs (292 lines) contains no occurrence of letterSpacing or letter-spacing, so the ramp check is size-and-leading only, and lessons.md has no tracking class, so this is a new defect and not a restated one. It breaks no constraint - it adds no hue, no weight, no family, and touches no architecture.
sharpenedFix: Confirm the defect, reject the first half of the fix. Do NOT move font-size out of b.css into render-b.js size utility classes: seven of the raises are `[data-medium="sheet"] .b-x` / `[data-medium="full"] .b-x` descendant rules, so a JS-applied .t-24 class cannot know it is on a sheet without duplicating the whole medium cascade in the renderer, and it would push presentation into the render layer for a one-off letterfit bug. Do the surgical half only, and enforce it: (1) in b.css pair every font-size with a letter-spacing in the same rule - add letter-spacing: var(--track-body) to .b-gapNote, .b-behindNote, .b-dayNote, .b-bubble, .b-undoAct, .b-emptyBody, .b-endedBody, .b-pressBody; add letter-spacing: var(--track-data) to .b-step. (2) In the min-width:701px block add letter-spacing: var(--track-head) to the .b-title and .b-when raises and var(--track-display) to the .b-dayNames raise. (3) For .b-emptyTitle at 64px use var(--track-title), do not declare a seventh step at -0.04em - shell.css's own comment reads 'Six steps and no seventh', and inventing a step to fit one heading is the same hand-tuning the ladder was built to stop; if 64px must sit in a band, widen the --track-title comment to 'sans 48-64px' rather than adding a value. (4) Two sizes fall outside the declared ladder and will fail any new assertion unless assigned first: .b-note at 13px and .b-unfurlHost at 12px sans, both currently 0em - fold them into --track-body and widen its comment to 'sans 12-20px', or state explicitly that sans below 15px is untracked. (5) Then extend audit.mjs with a size-wears-its-track assertion: for every rendered text element in the artifact, map computed fontSize+fontFamily to its ladder step and fail when the computed letterSpacing differs, and separately fail when one family+size renders at two different em tracks anywhere in the state matrix. Exempt visually-hidden nodes (.b-vh renders at 17px/normal and is screen-reader-only, so it must not be flagged) and exempt the console shell chrome, which is harness and not the artifact.
